courses.name: Programming Methodology II
structure: Canvas Home is a week-by-week timeline with links to diagnostics, problem sets, quiz/midterm/PE administration and the final. Check Announcements for changes and Assignments for official assessment details.

Canvas Pages contains course policy; Files contains problem sets and practice papers. The course's public units site provides teaching units, while Classroom50/GitHub are used for programming exercises and actual submission. A Canvas exercise page may say unsubmitted even when the work was submitted elsewhere.
Sit-in labs are physical calendar events, not planner actions; a concrete kit/preparation task may be actionable.

courses.name: Quantitative Reasoning with Data
structure: Canvas Home explains the blended format. Modules > ABOUT THE COURSE holds the teaching schedule; weekly Modules link lecture videos, tutorial material, quizzes and project information.

Files holds the group-project and video-assignment briefs and tutorial sheets. Announcements may point to newly released materials. Quizzes and Assignments provide official assessment state and deadlines.
Lecture videos are self-paced work; odd-week face-to-face tutorials require advance problem attempts, but attendance itself is calendar context.

courses.name: Changing Landscapes of Singapore
structure: Canvas Home opens Modules. The Welcome module's Syllabus, Assessment Components & Due Dates page is the primary assessment overview. Assignments and Group Project Forms modules contain the actual briefs and forms; weekly modules hold lecture content and release gates.

There is no visible Files or Pages tab. Course-wide Files/Pages list APIs can fail, but individual Module-linked Page slugs and File IDs are readable; follow those links. Announcements carry changes such as final-test rules.
Week 7 and later module content can be locked until its release date. Odd-week tutorials are physical; released self-paced lecture content and concrete preparation may be actionable.

courses.name: IT, Management and Organisation
structure: Canvas Home contains the assessment weights and a tentative week-by-week lesson/quiz plan. The syllabus and project specification are linked there and in Files; the project has separate proposal, presentation and report stages.

Use Quizzes and Assignments to confirm actual release and deadlines; a Home schedule alone is not proof a future quiz is open. Announcements often clarify active quiz and project dates. Syllabus and Pages are also available.
Lectures are physical calendar events; required preparation and project stages are actions.

courses.name: Introductory Mathematics
structure: Canvas Home gives assessment weights, midterm/final times and links to Course Schedule and weekly Pages. Weekly Pages and Files hold the session plan, lecture notes, recorded-preparation links and quiz sheets.
Announcements and Discussions can override the older schedule; the 22 September midterm announcement narrows coverage beyond the schedule. Use current announcements for corrections.
Watch assigned recordings before physical classes. In-class pen-and-paper quizzes are physical events, not separate outside-work todos; preparation may be actionable.

notes: GEA1000 and GESS1001 released self-paced lectures are actionable.
Physical classes are calendar context; concrete preparation is actionable.
GESS1001 and GEA1000 tutorials use the odd-week timetable.
